title: Specified completed tensor constraints descend through continuous realization
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, and $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $T$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme. On its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], for each finite $E\subset\Omega$ put $B_{E,T}=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_T$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], $E_T=B_{E,T}[1/\varpi_E]$, and $R_T=p_T^*\underline\Omega$, where $\underline\Omega(S)$ consists of continuous functions on a profinite set $S$ valued in one finite subextension [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed, sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x]. Write $\mathcal C_E(T)=D^b_c(T,E)$ for the raw rationalization of derived-complete integral constructible complexes, with its specified completed finite scalar transitions $S_{F/E}$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. Write $\mathcal C_T$ for the common-stage pair category of these $\mathcal C_E(T)$, with Hom groups the directed colimits over common finite fields [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. For $A=E_T,R_T$, let $\mathcal D_T(A)$ be the full subcategory of $D(\operatorname{Mod}(A))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of bounded objects whose cohomology sheaves have a finite locally closed stratification on each stratum of which they are pro-etale locally finite free over $A$.

Let $J_{E,T}=E_T\otimes^L_{B_{E,T}}-$ on integral representatives and let $\rho_T:\mathcal C_T\to\mathcal D_T(R_T)$ be the functor obtained by further extension to $R_T$, with balanced identity/tower comparisons. Use exactly the completed tensor, unit, reassociation, unitors and signed symmetry of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. For integral constructible $K,L$, let $\chi_{K,L}:K\otimes^L_{B_{E,T}}L\to K\widehat\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}L$ be the specified quotient-tower comparison [lem-fix-constructible-tensor-completion]. Define
$$\mu_{E;K,L}:J_{E,T}K\otimes^L_{E_T}J_{E,T}L\longrightarrow J_{E,T}(K\widehat\otimes^L L)$$
as balanced scalar multiplication followed by $J_{E,T}(\chi_{K,L})$; the multiplication map on K-flat representatives is $(a\otimes x)\otimes(b\otimes y)\mapsto ab\otimes(x\otimes y)$, with inverse $a\otimes(x\otimes y)\mapsto(a\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$ before applying $\chi$.

These maps are isomorphisms natural in $K,L$ and respect the actual completed associator, both action unitors and signed symmetry. More precisely coherent reduction of each constraint square through $\chi$ is the corresponding whole-system total-complex map: reassociation $(x\otimes y)\otimes z\mapsto x\otimes(y\otimes z)$, action $b\otimes x\mapsto bx$ or $x\otimes b\mapsto bx$, or swap $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$. This identifies the specified constraints even for iterated completed tensors with re-resolved inner expressions.

Rationalization of $\mu_E$ and extension from a common finite field to $R_T$ give a well-defined tensorator $\mu_{M,N}:\rho_TM\otimes^L_{R_T}\rho_TN\xrightarrow{\sim}\rho_T(M\otimes N)$, independent of field and arrow representatives. Tensor of pure rational arrows multiplies the scalar coefficients. The tensorator respects balanced finite scalar comparison, including its identity and tower maps, and makes $\rho_T$ symmetric strong monoidal. The unit comparison is the multiplication $R_T\otimes_{E_T}E_T\cong R_T$.

proof.text: Apply lem-sf-adic-finite-realization-cocone to $T$. It identifies the integral category used by $\mathcal C_E(T)$ with the bounded constructible complete category, with the same morphisms and reductions; it also identifies the stated constructibility conventions for $E_T,R_T$. Moreover $T$ is qcqs and $\ell$ is invertible, so lem-fix-constructible-tensor-completion applies to these very integral representatives. Thus the specified $\chi_{K,L}$ is a natural isomorphism. Apply the ordinary derived scalar tensor comparison to the identity geometric morphism with ring map $B_{E,T}\to E_T$. On flat-term K-flat representatives this comparison is the cochain comparison $c$ of lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence, whose stated inverse is the balanced multiplication $(a\otimes x)\otimes(b\otimes y)\mapsto ab\otimes(x\otimes y)$, so composing it with $J_E(\chi_{K,L})$ gives exactly $\mu_E$ in the statement. Both factors are natural isomorphisms. Completed tensor remains integral constructible by lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible, so the codomain belongs to the stated category.

proof.text: Use coherent reductions $A=\mathcal RK$, $N=\mathcal RL$, and $H=\mathcal RM$. Their transition adjoints are the derived scalar associators, hence invertible; these are normalized systems. Tensor expressions remain normalized because derived scalar extension is monoidal (lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence), so each induced transition adjoint is a tensor of invertible adjoints. The primitive tensor comparisons of lem-pur-completed-primitive-counit-comparison are invertible, and so are their recursive composites on every finite tensor expression. The normalized effectivity counit is invertible at each such system, hence so is each $\gamma_P=e_{S_P}\mathcal R(\beta_P)$. Apply lem-pur-normalized-tensor-constraint-transport: the actual completed constraint is $\beta_Q^{-1}\mathcal L(a)\beta_P$ and $\gamma_Q\mathcal R(\widehat a)=a\gamma_P$, with $a$ the stated reassociation, either action, or signed swap. This uses a simultaneous whole-system comparison; it does not infer equality from unrelated levelwise isomorphisms. The primitive comparisons are resolution independent, so the same assertion holds when an inner completed tensor is re-resolved.

proof.text: To identify these comparisons through the particular $\chi$, use lem-pur-integral-ambient-operation-models: completion of the ordinary total tensor is identified with the completed quotient tensor by the balanced maps of entire strict towers, preserving their quotient augmentations and zero shifted coordinates. Thus $\chi$ is that augmentation followed by this identification. Naturality of the cochain tensor comparisons makes its reassociation, action and swap squares the maps $a$ of step 2. Consequently the ordinary constraints are taken to the actual completed constraints through $\chi$. Ordinary scalar extension is symmetric strong monoidal by lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons. Composing its multiplication tensorator with $J_E(\chi)$ therefore gives all the required constraint equations for $\mu_E$, including both unitors.

proof.text: For $E\subset F$, use $j_{F/E}$ of lem-sf-adic-finite-realization-cocone and the specified scalar comparison for completed tensor in lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension. To check their tensor square, replace completed scalar extension by the inverse of $\chi_{F/E}$ from lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison. It is the quotient augmentation with zero shifted coordinate. The completed tensor scalar comparison itself is pinned by lem-pur-scalar-extension-tower-coherence: it is the derived limit of the strict quotient-tower tensor scalar-extension maps $\sigma_W$, $(x\otimes y)\otimes b\mapsto(x\otimes b)\otimes(y\otimes1)$, with their identity and successive-extension equations. Step 3 identifies the tensor augmentations in the same way. The remaining square is therefore the balanced cochain scalar square of lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence: on homogeneous inputs it multiplies the same two coefficient scalars and leaves $x\otimes y$ unchanged. The equality holds on entire quotient towers and hence after their functorial derived limits. This also checks the unit square, where the formula is multiplication. For identity and successive finite extensions the comparisons $j$ already obey the actual identity/tower equations; their compatibility with tensor is the monoidality of scalar composition in lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons. No equality of the two uniformizer filtrations is used: $\chi_{F/E}$ uses the actual $F$-uniformizer quotient tower.

proof.text: Localize the integral Hom modules as in def-weil-rationalization-karoubi and lem-sf-scalar-localization-monoidal. On pure arrows $(u\otimes a),(v\otimes b)$ the tensor is $(u\widehat\otimes v)\otimes ab$. Map a rational arrow under $J_E$ to $aJ_E(u)$. Naturality of $\mu_E$ then extends to pure rational arrows because both routes are $ab$ times the integral naturality equation; additivity gives the equation for sums. Balancing over $\mathcal O_E$ is respected by linearity. Inverse comparison components localize as well, so $\mu_E$ remains invertible. Every constraint and scalar square proved above is an equality of integral arrows and therefore remains an equality after this localization.

For $M=(E,K)$ and $N=(F,L)$ choose $G\supset E,F$. Extend the rational $\mu_G$ on $S_{G/E}K,S_{G/F}L$ to $R_T$ and conjugate by $j_{G/E},j_{G/F}$ and the tensor transition comparison; this defines the proposed $\mu_{M,N}$. Step 4 says that replacing $G$ by $G'\supset G$ gives the same map after the specified cocone comparisons. Two arbitrary choices compare at a further common extension. For arrows choose one finite field representing both arrows and the objects concerned. Their naturality square is the scalar extension of the rational square of step 5. If either representative is changed, the two representatives agree at some further common field by def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients, where these squares agree. Thus the tensorator is independent of object-stage choices and arrow representatives and is natural for every common-stage arrow. Its inverse is obtained in exactly the same way from $\mu_G^{-1}$.

Every associativity, symmetry, unitor, or finite scalar compatibility diagram has finitely many objects and arrows. Represent all of them over one common finite field. By steps 3–5 the corresponding finite-stage diagram commutes, and extension to $R_T$ preserves this equality. Step 6 identifies its edges with the tensorator just constructed, including the specified identity and tower maps. These are precisely the symmetric strong monoidal equations for $\rho_T$. The coefficient object at that field is $E_T$; its comparison after extension is $R_T\otimes_{E_T}E_T\to R_T$, $r\otimes e\mapsto re$, with inverse $r\mapsto r\otimes1$. This is the required unit normalization.
